# ACF Framework Documentation — crawler policy
#
# Generated by scripts/build-crawler-files.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
# Enforced by tests/crawler-contract.test.mjs.
#
# The eleven clean routes are the indexable surface, and each declares its own
# canonical. Duplicate suppression for the RAW /site-b/**.html documents that
# back them is owned by ONE mechanism: `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, set on those
# documents in next.config.mjs.
#
# This file therefore disallows nothing under /site-b/. That is deliberate, and
# it corrects a rule that used to read `Disallow: /site-b/` and was described
# here as "belt and braces" with the header. It was the opposite of that, in two
# ways. A header can only be read by a crawler that is allowed to fetch the
# document carrying it, so disallowing the path did not reinforce the noindex —
# it prevented it from ever being seen, which is exactly the case Google
# documents as leaving a URL eligible for indexing from external links alone.
# And the same one line covered every resource the canonical pages need: the
# stylesheets, the scripts, the fonts, the JSON the runtime reads, and the
# social cards named by og:image. Rendered as a compliant crawler saw it, the
# framework-in-pictures page kept 585 of its 9,110 words, a part page lost 30%,
# every page fell back to Times New Roman, and no chart exhibit drew at all.
#
# So: fetch anything the documentation needs; index only the clean routes; and
# keep the server-side API closed.

User-agent: *
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/

Sitemap: https://docs.acfdashboard.com/sitemap.xml
